$comment: The upstream review ledger - version2.md section 7.1.
Every entry is a version somebody CHOSE. 'pinned' is what this project uses today;
'reviewed.upstream' is what upstream was serving the last time a person looked, and it is
the only field the detector compares against. When a live probe answers something else, that
entry has MOVED and owes a decision before the next release: re-pin it deliberately, or
upgrade it and validate against the suite.
Nothing here fails a build. 'dotnet run --project tools/FrameLink.Upstream -- check' is the
detector, and no build, test or publish invokes it. The only always-on check is the offline
test that keeps this file agreeing with the pins in source, which fails when a human changed
one and forgot the other - never because upstream published something overnight.
Debian package versions are deliberately NOT in scope. The apt resources move forward on
their own through security updates, by design, and the Fleet Manager records the versions it
finds. Recorded inventory is not a chosen version: an entry per Debian package would turn a
release gate into a daily chore, and a ceremony nobody performs is worse than none.

entries.title: Raspberry Pi OS Lite (Trixie, arm64) - the base image the section 3.9 generator writes into

reviewed.note: Measured against the file the URL served on 2026-08-15: the published .sha256 sidecar matched, the archive decompressed to the recorded length, and the image digest, the partition table and the three target directories were read back out of the result. Upstream publishes each image under a directory dated a day after the image itself - raspios_lite_arm64-2026-06-19 holds the 2026-06-18 image - so the probe's answer and the pin differ by that day and always will.

entries.title: Immich Kiosk - the slideshow the agent fetches and supervises (section 2.1, decision 41)

reviewed.note: Re-probed live on 2026-08-15 while the kiosk.binary.pinned-release resource was written, so this entry now points at the pin in source rather than at a paragraph. The release API answers v0.42.0 (published 2026-08-04); immich-kiosk_0.42.0_checksums.txt names 93476535e86dd6914b1b8e644fdc147b4770903434f0db15d0ee469e0857e423 for immich-kiosk_Linux_arm64.tar.gz and the 7,712,323 downloaded bytes hash to it; the archive holds LICENSE, README.md and one 18,546,850-byte immich-kiosk at 0755 whose Go build record reads -X main.version=0.42.0 with GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0. KioskReleasePin carries both digests because they answer different questions: the published one gates the download, the binary one is what the resource observes on the frame every pass. One thing upstream does not offer is a bind address - main.go starts the server on ':' plus the port and the config struct has no host field - so the loopback-only property v1 had was Docker's port publishing, not Kiosk's, and kiosk.listen-address records the real bind set rather than claiming it. v1's compose file still names 0.39.3 and is not a consumer of anything v2 builds.

entries.title: LiveKit server - the call server the Fleet Manager fetches and supervises (section 3.7)

reviewed.note: Probed live on 2026-08-16 while section 3.7's bundled path was written, so this entry points at the pin in source rather than at a paragraph. The release API answers v1.13.5 (published 2026-07-31T06:59:38Z, not a prerelease); checksums.txt names c020fac437b7cc9b776eef1ad5ea8af77be9acfa07602eca20a3a44930dfbc70 for livekit_1.13.5_linux_amd64.tar.gz and 332015305518765fe05bad74fc3a9d9583e635e7dd130de3c4fc563d69c550f3 for the arm64 archive, and the 18,064,127 and 16,349,520 downloaded bytes hash to exactly those. Each archive holds two members - LICENSE (11,358 bytes, Apache License 2.0) and a livekit-server executable at 0755 - and both binaries' Go build records read -X main.version=1.13.5 -X main.commit=3b9f118327b257301083a7c4aa46076c8012918a with CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux and go1.26.5, which is where 'static Go binary' is checked rather than assumed. LiveKitReleasePin carries four digests because they answer different questions: the two published ones gate each download, the two measured binary ones are what the installer re-checks on every start. Both Linux architectures are pinned because the Fleet Manager's own platform is the operator's choice; the Windows and macOS assets upstream also publishes are deliberately absent. The amd64 binary was then run under debian:trixie-slim: it accepted the exact configuration LiveKitConfigFile renders and answered 'ports' with 7880 HTTP, 7881 ICE/TCP and 50000-50199 ICE/UDP, it refused a config carrying one unknown key (so every field in that file is a real one), and a token minted by LiveKitToken was answered 200 success by /rtc/validate while an expired one and one signed with a rotated secret were both answered 401. v1's guide 7 pulled the livekit/livekit-server:v1.13.3 container image and is not a consumer of anything v2 builds.

entries.title: reSpeaker XVF3800 host control tool - the six files the agent fetches to talk to the mic array (decision 63)

reviewed.note: Probed live on 2026-08-16 while decision 63 was taken, so this entry points at the pin in source rather than at a paragraph. This is the entry the github-path-commit probe kind was added for: the repository has zero releases and zero tags, /releases/latest answers 404, and the artifact is loose files on a moving master branch - so github-release cannot answer for it at all, and an upstream that silently cannot be checked is worse than one that is not registered. commits?path=host_control/rpi_64bit&per_page=1 answers 200 with 725f38464e73477a30aba9f5c220f1cfdc66d682, committed 2025-07-04T08:41:12Z, and that is the event worth watching: Seeed rebuilding the tool. Six files were downloaded from raw.githubusercontent.com at that SHA and each hashes to what XvfHostReleasePin carries - xvf_host 63f89c6672c0d89bc82d8182cb36013ac3619288780f315a2e0373fb3ed771f2 (1,772,904 bytes), libcommand_map.so c1b424313e48cfe97c5cfce0530ac05fe47f818cc0fba15a9954198ef105282c (151,680), libdevice_i2c.so 7acb02a6ae14c34e3291fb55ec91d681d2902b79916df9fef53b5501fc2d1b3b (72,568), libdevice_usb.so 5b52ee35ef17aa287555abb112ebb1dc8497e11d43acc1bd223170d02e28eddd (73,312), dfu_cmds.yaml 67f6a982567b8d23da85c5806c40344094d21071c631344a47164cd085dddba3 (2,507) and transport_config.yaml 071f1fb87cfbdeffd3ba624713fa0745f27debfbde0544e8ac1af3863c29034d (30). The same six downloaded from today's master head (a652fe79da3a292b25decc0e1e7f267d29bb0284) are byte-for-byte identical, so the directory has been frozen for the thirteen months the repository around it kept moving. A raw URL carrying a full commit SHA is content-addressed, which is what makes a pin possible with no release to point at; the digests are measured here rather than published, because this publisher publishes none - the same weakness a checksums.txt has, since nobody signs one either. Six files and not four: the catalog used to name the binary and three .so files, and Seeed's own host_control/README.md lists dfu_cmds.yaml and transport_config.yaml as required members of the same directory. The seventh file there, xvf_i2c_dfu, is deliberately not fetched - this build does USB DFU through dfu-util and never the I2C path. Nothing is vendored: the repository carries no licence file at all (0 of 19 blobs at this commit, 0 of 51 at head), so redistribution is unlicensed, and the XMOS licence the tool appears to be built under forbids making the software available on a standalone basis while expressly permitting shipping it installed on the devices. The probe watches the directory rather than the six files, so a change to xvf_i2c_dfu would also report as moved - deliberately over-sensitive, because a human reads a moved entry and a missed rebuild reaches a frame. v1's guide 4 obtained these same files by an unpinned git clone --depth 1 of the whole repository and is not a consumer of anything v2 builds.

entries.title: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite - the Fleet Manager's store, EF Core being unusable under AOT (section 6.2)

reviewed.note: Floats by section 7.1: the reference is Version="*", and restore resolved 10.0.11 on 2026-08-15, which is what nuget.org served that day. A float cannot be held back without becoming a pin, so this entry moves the moment nuget.org does - which is the whole point of watching it, because the next build takes the new one whether or not anyone looked.

entries.title: xunit.v3 - the suite runner both the harness and the operator invoke

reviewed.note: Floats by section 7.1, resolved 4.0.0 on 2026-08-15. Worth a human's attention on every move rather than a shrug: 4.0.0 is the version whose dropped VSTest bridge is why the suite runs by executing the project directly instead of through dotnet test, and a runner change lands underneath every other gate in this repository.

entries.title: .NET LTS band - the target framework both programs are built against

reviewed.note: What is chosen here is the band, not the patch: net10.0 is LTS, in active support, EOL 2028-11-14, and .NET 8 and 9 were both out of support from 2026-11-10 (section 6.2). The probe answers with the channel's newest SDK, 10.0.400 on 2026-08-15; the workstation that built this ran 10.0.302 (section 6.1), which is a build-host fact rather than an artifact one, since Native AOT leaves no runtime for the frame to have. A support phase that stops being 'active' is the signal this entry exists to deliver.
